title: foresightr
text: Previsão de séries temporais em R que escolhe o modelo pelo que teria dado certo. O foresightr ajusta vários modelos uma série, refaz o passado para ver como cada um teria se saído, escolhe pelo erro fora da amostra e dá faixas tiradas dos erros de fato observados, inclusive para o total dos próximos k períodos. Os modelos, o backtest e ferramentas são o crate Rust foresight, compilado dentro pacote: os números são os crate e o backtest usa todos os núcleos. O lado R não depende de nada além R base. Site: https://strategicprojects.github.io/foresightr/

title: foresightr
text: instalação pelo código-fonte compila o Rust e precisa dele (https://rustup.rs); Windows, também alvo GNU: rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-gnu.
code: remotes::install_github("StrategicProjects/foresightr")

title: foresightr
code: library(foresightr) bt <- backtest(AirPassengers)   # 36 origens, 12 meses à frente, 11 modelos bt$forecast                     # previsão com faixas de 80% e 95% total_forecast(bt, 6)           # total dos próximos seis meses, com faixa própria plot(bt)

title: foresightr
text: Modelos: média, ingênuo, tendência, sazonal ingênuo, Theta, Holt-Winters, regressão log-linear (com deflator opcional), ARIMA sazonal por máxima verossimilhança exata (com regressores), ARIMA automático, família ETS com escolha automática, Prophet (quebras de tendência, eventos e degraus), TBATS e Croston, SBA e TSB para demanda intermitente. Decomposição STL e MSTL, e qualquer modelo sobre série dessazonalizada. Ensemble: média, mediana, pesos pelo inverso erro ou pesos empilhados. Limpeza: preenchimento de falhas e troca de valores atípicos. Backtest por origem móvel em todos os núcleos, com MAPE, MAE, RMSE, MASE e viés por horizonte e faixas empíricas. Os números são os crate Rust, conferido com os pacotes forecast e prophet R; os mesmos métodos existem em Python (pyforesight) e Go (foresight-go).

title: Decomposition and cleaning
text: decompose_stl() splits series trend, seasonal pattern remainder LOESS. defaults stats::stl(), numbers.  strengths, 0 1, say much variation trend seasonal pattern explain; seasonal_strength() computes latter directly. robust = TRUE -weights outliers.
code: d <- decompose_stl(log(AirPassengers), seasonal_window = 13) d #> <foresight decomposition> 144 observations, period 12 #> Strength of the trend: 0.996 #> Strength of seasonality (12): 0.961 plot(d)

title: Decomposition and cleaning
text: Daily data often weekly monthly pattern. decompose_mstl() estimates turn:  decomposition serves forecast: model_decomposed() runs model seasonally adjusted series adds patterns back.
code: t <- 0:419 weekly <- c(5, 0, -2, -3, 0, 1, -1) daily <- 100 + 0.05 * t + weekly[t %% 7 + 1] + 8 * sin(2 * pi * t / 30) +   2 * sin(t * 1.7) * cos(t * 0.3) d <- decompose_mstl(daily, periods = c(7, 30)) d$seasonal_strength #>  seasonal_7 seasonal_30  #>   0.8464823   0.9687255 plot(d) model <- model_decomposed(model_drift(), periods = c(7, 30)) f <- forecast_model(model, daily, 14, period = 7) round(f, 1) #>  [1] 127.5 124.1 123.6 124.2 128.3 130.4 129.4 135.8 130.5 128.3 126.9 128.7 #> [13] 128.5 125.4

title: Decomposition and cleaning
text: fill_gaps() fills missing values following seasonal pattern; clean_series() also replaces outliers: Models require complete series, cleaning comes first data gaps. Whether outlier replaced judgement data: strike really happened, removing may hide risk happen .
code: y <- log(AirPassengers) y[30] <- y[30] + 0.8     # a typing error y[100] <- y[100] - 0.7   # a strike y[61:62] <- NA           # months never recorded find_outliers(y) #>   index     time    value replacement #> 1    30 1951.417 5.981784    5.217194 #> 2    52 1953.250 5.459586    5.430423 #> 3   100 1957.250 5.152202    5.855171 #> 4   135 1960.167 6.037871    6.146164 cleaned <- clean_series(y) round(exp(cbind(dirty = y, clean = cleaned)[c(30, 61, 62, 100), ])) #>      dirty clean #> [1,]   396   184 #> [2,]    NA   207 #> [3,]    NA   199 #> [4,]   173   349

title: Regressors and events
text: Tax revenue follows prices. log price index regressor, errors regression follow ARIMA model, estimated together. model fitted first 100 months, index covers 12 months forecast. regressors argument taken model_arima() model_auto_arima(), data frame, matrix named list one row per period first observation .
code: model <- model_arima(c(0, 1, 1), c(0, 1, 1),                      regressors = data.frame(ipca = log(data$ipca_index))) fit <- fit_model(model, log(window(icms, end = time(icms)[100]))) fit$details$regression #>     ipca  #> 3.630129 exp(predict(fit, 6)) #>           Jul      Aug      Sep      Oct      Nov      Dec #> 2025 755.1627 755.8939 770.2862 789.3318 772.8459 800.0233

title: Regressors and events
text: Sine cosine pairs describe seasonal pattern parameters, period need whole number. fourier_terms() gives many rows needed: seasonal_dummies() gives one dummy per season instead; combine sets regressors cbind().
code: y <- log(AirPassengers) x <- fourier_terms(12, 3, length(y) + 12) fit <- fit_model(model_arima(c(1, 1, 1), constant = TRUE, regressors = x), y) names(fit$details$regression) #> [1] "sin1_12" "cos1_12" "sin2_12" "cos2_12" "sin3_12" "cos3_12" round(exp(predict(fit, 12))) #>      Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec #> 1961 451 473 499 513 523 574 654 666 575 487 465 484

title: Regressors and events
text: Prophet-style model takes events, happen given positions (counted 1 first observation, future ones included), steps, lasting changes level position . effects estimated trend seasonality. effects come close +20 -15 put , forecast includes campaign planned position 131.
code: set.seed(1) t <- 1:120 sales <- 200 + 0.8 * t + 5 * sin(2 * pi * t / 12) + rnorm(120, sd = 2) campaigns <- c(11, 35, 59, 83, 107) sales[campaigns] <- sales[campaigns] + 20     # a campaign every other November sales[t >= 81] <- sales[t >= 81] - 15          # a new law cuts the level sales <- ts(sales, frequency = 12)  model <- model_prophet(changepoints = 0,                        events = list(campaign = c(campaigns, 131)),                        steps = list(new_law = 81)) fit <- fit_model(model, sales) round(fit$details$effects, 1) #> campaign  new_law  #>     19.8    -14.8
